verses.text: A few days later, Jesus returned to Capernaum. Word got around that he was home,
and so many people gathered that there wasn’t room even outside the door. He was sharing God’s message with them.
Some people came, carrying a paralyzed man. Four of them were carrying him.
They couldn’t get him to Jesus because of the crowd, so they opened the roof above Jesus. After digging through it, they lowered the mat the paralyzed man was lying on.
When Jesus saw their faith, he said to the man, “Child, your sins are forgiven.”
Some legal experts were sitting there, thinking to themselves,
“Why is he talking like this? That’s blasphemy! Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
Jesus immediately knew in his spirit what they were thinking, so he said, “Why are you thinking this in your hearts?
Which is easier: to tell this paralyzed man, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up, pick up your mat, and walk’?
But I want you to know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins.” Then he said to the paralyzed man,
“I’m telling you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
The man got up, picked up his mat, and walked out in front of everyone. They were all amazed and praised God, saying, “We’ve never seen anything like this!”
Jesus went out again beside the lake. The crowd came to him, and he taught them.
As he walked along, he saw Levi son of Alphaeus sitting at the tax booth. Jesus said to him, “Follow me.” Levi got up and followed him.
Later, Jesus was eating at Levi’s house. Many tax collectors and sinners were eating with him and his disciples, because many of them were following him.
When the legal experts from the Pharisees saw Jesus eating with sinners and tax collectors, they asked his disciples, “Why does he eat with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus heard them and said, “Healthy people don’t need a doctor; sick people do. I didn’t come to call righteous people, but sinners.”
John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting. Some people came and asked Jesus, “Why do John’s disciples and the Pharisees’ disciples fast, but yours don’t?”
Jesus answered, “Can wedding guests fast while the groom is with them? As long as they have the groom with them, they can’t fast.
But the time will come when the groom is taken away from them. On that day, they’ll fast.
No one patches an old coat with unshrunk cloth. Otherwise, the patch pulls away from it, new from old, and the tear gets worse.
And no one pours new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the wine will burst the skins, and both the wine and the skins will be ruined. Instead, new wine belongs in fresh wineskins.”
One Sabbath, Jesus and his disciples were walking through grainfields. As they went, the disciples began picking heads of grain.
The Pharisees said to him, “Look, why are they doing what isn’t allowed on the Sabbath?”
He answered, “Haven’t you ever read what David did when he and his companions were hungry and had nothing to eat?
He went into God’s house during the time Abiathar was high priest and ate the bread set out before God—which only priests are allowed to eat—and he also gave some to his companions.”
Then he said, “The Sabbath was made for people, not people for the Sabbath.
So the Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
